title: scale-policy-impact-tracking-multi-region-may-2026
body:
Scale Policy Impact Tracker - Multi-region experiments (May 2026)

Tab: summary (this sheet)
Columns: Experiment ID, Region, GPU Type, Pool, Min nodes, Max nodes, Scale up trigger (metric), Up threshold, Scale down trigger (metric), Down threshold, Cooldown (s), Workload profile, Avg tokens/s, Observed p95 latency (ms), Cost delta vs baseline (%), Incident count (5d), Notes, Recommended action

Rows:
EXP-0601, us-west1, A10G, general-purpose, 2, 20, request_rate, 220 rps, idle_time, 45s, 120, steady-high-queries, 210, 260, +12%, 0, Aggressive up trigger hit quickly during morning spikes; p95 rose at tails when cold-starts occurred; consider pre-warm policy for 06:00-10:00 PST, schedule canary
EXP-0602, us-east1, A100, high-throughput, 4, 40, gpu_utilization, 0.78, gpu_utilization, 0.45, 180, bursty-batch, 480, 180, -6%, 1, Reduced cost but one scale-lag incident during large batched eval job; cooldown too long for bursty job pattern; lower cooldown to 90s and add request-based fallback
EXP-0603, eu-west1, A100, reserved-low, 1, 8, request_rate, 95 rps, request_rate, 40 rps, 240, low-steady, 60, 130, +3%, 0, Stable but underutilized during nights; consider shifting some low-priority jobs to spot pools or increase min to reduce tail latency for interactive sessions
EXP-0604, ap-southeast1, H100, gpu-intensive, 6, 48, combined (gpu_util + rps), up if either >70% or >350 rps, down if both <50% and <150 rps, 120, spiky-ml-training, 960, 410, +22%, 2, Fast ramps during training checkpoints triggered rapid scale-ups; observed failures when burst exceeded max capacity; add burst-capacity reserve and autoscaler preemption policy
EXP-0605, us-central1, A10G, mixed, 3, 24, request_rate, 300 rps, request_rate, 90 rps, 90, mixed-sla, 320, 215, -2%, 0, Balanced cost + latency; cooldown of 90s seemed best compromise; occasional oscillation around the down threshold at troughs — add hysteresis (tiered thresholds)
EXP-0606, eu-north1, A100, experiment-pool, 2, 12, latency_p99, 950 ms, latency_p99, 650 ms, 300, latency-sensitive, 140, 1100, +8%, 1, Using p99 as trigger reduced end-user tail but increased baseline spend; recommend using p95 for auto-scaling and reserve small buffer nodes for p99 fallback
EXP-0607, us-west2, A10G, dev-sandbox, 0, 6, request_rate, 40 rps, request_rate, 10 rps, 45, dev, 22, 480, -30%, 0, Low priority pool; cost savings prioritized; observed frequent spin-ups; add longer cool-down + maintaining 1 warm node during business hours
EXP-0608, ap-northeast1, A100, dedicated-enterprise, 8, 64, gpu_utilization, 0.85, gpu_utilization, 0.5, 240, enterprise-sla, 820, 175, +5%, 0, High throughput with strict latency targets. Scale behaved predictably but costs higher; propose negotiated reserved capacity commit or increasing bin packing efficiency

Quick metrics and formulas used (sheet formulas, placed in notes column):
- Avg tokens/s: measured over 5d sliding window sampled at 1m resolution
- Cost delta vs baseline: (observed_cost - baseline_cost)/baseline_cost * 100
- Incident count: number of customer-facing errors or infra alerts attributed to scaling during experiment window

Observations (bullet list)
- Trigger type matters: request_rate triggers react fastest to traffic spikes; gpu_utilization triggers are smoother for long-running batches but slower to react to sudden headroom needs. Combined triggers reduce false positives but add complexity.
- Cooldown tuning is workload-dependent: short cooldowns (<=90s) are good for mixed/interactive workloads; long cooldowns (>180s) reduce oscillation for batch-heavy workloads.
- Hysteresis/higher thresholds needed at lower mins: pools with min <=2 saw frequent cold-start latency spikes; recommendation to maintain at least 1 warm node in interactive pools.
- Burst capacity and reserve are essential for training/checkpoint patterns in H100 pools — hitting max_nodes causes request failures.
- Cost vs latency trade-offs are non-linear by region due to pricing and preemptible availability. ap-southeast and ap-northeast showed highest cost jumps for aggressive scale-ups.

Conclusions and recommended actions:
- Standardize two policy templates: interactive-template (min>=1, request_rate trigger, up threshold 200-350 rps, cooldown 60-120s, hysteresis tiers) and batch-template (min>=2, gpu_utilization trigger, up threshold 0.7, cooldown 180-300s).
- Implement combined-trigger mode for training pools: primary gpu_utilization + secondary request_rate as emergency ramp.
- Add pre-warm windows for region-specific business hours (US mornings, EU afternoons, AP evenings). Use scheduled scaling instead of only reactive for predictable daily ramps.
- For enterprise/dedicated pools, offer a smaller reserved buffer (3-5 nodes) to reduce tail SLA breaches; technical sales to model cost vs commit levels.
- Update autoscaler docs and deploy playbook changes behind feature flag; run A/B test against current baseline for 30 days with telemetry focused on p95 latency and cost_per_token.

Action items (owners):
- Priya Nair: create RFC for interactive-template and batch-template and land autoscaler feature-flag (due 2026-06-10)
- Ethan Cole: implement pre-warm schedule prototype for us-west1 and measure delta (due 2026-06-17)
- Maya Rodriguez: run A/B cost/regression test across three representative pools (EXP-0601, EXP-0602, EXP-0604) and produce report (due 2026-07-01)
- Luca Bianchi: add telemetry hooks for combined-trigger events and scale-failure reason codes (due 2026-06-24)

Notes-to-self / open questions
- How much of observed cost delta is driven by instance startup GPU pricing vs per-minute billing granularity? Need finance to breakdown.
- Should we expand combined-trigger to include queue-depth for queued inference? Product input needed.
- Does committing small reserved capacity for enterprise customers reduce overall committed spend or just shift costs? Sales + Finance modeling required.
